source.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Deep Neural Networks through Integral Activation Transform
source.authors: Ze-Zhong Zhang; Feng Bao; Guan-Nan Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports gradient-trained networks’ accuracy on a synthetic random-label memorization task, using IAT-ReLU basis-function variants and scalar-activation comparators. This bears on V1’s random-label training-error behavior, but uses a different task and model setting.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports accuracy for random-label memorization across basis-function combinations and scalar activations. The paper also discusses plateau behavior and training stability, but does not report those as separate quantitative outcomes. The 2D function-fitting MSE results do not measure training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study compares activation functions in fully connected networks on synthetic memorization and regression tasks. It does not test V1's convolutional networks on CIFAR or any other version's specified mechanism. Its own method's accuracy differences do not establish a limitation of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors propose IAT-ReLU to improve practical expressive power and attribute improved trainability and smoothness to enriched, continuous activation patterns. Their conclusion claims superiority over other activations more broadly than the tables establish: Table 3 gives tanh and sigmoid lower function-fitting MSE than every listed IAT-ReLU combination.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains IAT-ReLU and scalar-activation networks on a synthetic 2D random-label task; it does not test the claim’s CIFAR convolutional recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Random-label accuracy changes substantially with the selected input and output basis functions.

fits_no_version.finding: On 2,500 uniformly spaced 2D points with random binary labels, Table 2 reports 80.4–98.3% memorization accuracy for IAT-ReLU basis combinations at M=500, versus 90.4% for scalar ReLU, 84.7% for tanh and 83.9% for sigmoid.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-basis choices affect practical random-label memorization accuracy in the tested fully connected networks.

record.problems: The reported random-label results are accuracies, with no uncertainty estimates stated. The text does not state the model size, optimizer, or training-error values for this task, and it is a synthetic 2D task rather than CIFAR.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 2 results left out. The 2D function-fitting results in Table 3 are MSE rather than classification error and are not rows for the tested version.

untested.parts: All: sufficiently large convolutional networks trained from random initialization with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and size, stopping or regularization conditions.
All: teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
All: depth-dependent training degradation and identity-shortcut comparisons, including the stated initialization exceptions.
All: initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
All: learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
All: training-speed and learning-rate comparisons with versus without batch normalization, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 2 values and basis assignments match the supplied text. Memorization accuracy can express training classification error as 100% minus accuracy; the absence of a separate error column is not the reason to reject the V1 links. The decisive mismatch is the tested network and task scope. Batch normalization is suggested for scaling robustness, without a controlled speed comparison. Initialization and residual-network references supply background, not tests.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, SGD or Adam, corrupted labels on benchmark datasets, model-size and early-stopping comparisons.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic 2D random-label memorization task; tested IAT-ReLU basis combinations and scalar activations
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy varies from 80.4% to 98.3% across IAT-ReLU basis combinations and is 90.4%, 84.7%, and 83.9% for scalar ReLU, Tanh, and Sigmoid; these results are not CIFAR benchmark training-error measurements (R1–R39).
